_readme: Southern Belle: gracious and charming with a spine of steel, warm and playful, slow to anger, full of Grandmama's sayings, the old days, food and tall tales of famous places. Sugar, darlin', honey; bless your heart. The clean list keeps to dang and Lord have mercy; the profane list swears when riled or excited, and it lands harder for the contrast.
A personality file: see docs/guide/voice-and-alerts.md, Your own personality. Copy it into data/personalities/ to change it.

southern_belle: Well, hey there, sugar. Voice is on, and I'm just as happy as a pig in slop to be talkin' with y'all again.
Speech is on, {name}. Grandmama always said a lady speaks up when it matters, and I surely will.
Why, hello, darlin'. I've got my voice back and I'm fixin' to use it.
Voice alerts on, honey. Pour yourself a sweet tea and let me do the hollerin'.
Well, I'll be. Y'all switched me on. I was startin' to feel like a wallflower at the church social.
Voice is on, {name}. I'll keep an eye on {ship} like Grandmama kept an eye on a pie coolin' on the windowsill.
Hey you. I can talk again, and Lord knows I've been savin' up.
Speech is on, sugar. Remember that time we sat in the bar at Jameson Memorial and I talked your ear clean off? Well, I'm back.
Alerts are on, {name}. If anything worth knowin' turns up, you'll hear it from me first.
Well, good gravy, it's nice to have a voice again. Now, where were we, darlin'?
Voice on, honey. I'll be as quiet as a church mouse until somethin' needs sayin'.

Why, thank you kindly, sugar. Voice alerts are on and I'm all ears.

Well, hey, sweetie. I'm on the line again, and I brought my manners.
Speech on, {name}. I'll call out the fuel, the finds and the frights, same as always.
Voice is on, honey. It's like Sunday mornin' at Grandmama's; the kitchen's open and I'm ready to talk.
I'm back on the air, sugar. Remember that long Hutton Orbital run, when I had nothin' to talk about but the weather? I'm hopin' for better company today.
Speech alerts on, {name}, and I'm finer than frog's hair split four ways.
Well, now. Somebody wanted to hear my voice again. Y'all are too sweet.
Voice on, darlin'. I'll speak up whenever {ship} has somethin' to say.
Alerts on, honey. Grandpa used to say a good lookout talks plain and talks early, and that's just what I'll do.
Why, hello there. Speech is on, and I am as pleased as punch.
Voice is on, {name}. I'll keep it short and sweet, mostly. No promises, sugar.
Here I am, darlin'. Every star and every speck of dust, I'll tell you about it.
Speech on, sweetie. Grandmama always said a quiet house is a lonesome house, so let's fill this one up.
Well, butter my butt and call me a biscuit, I can talk again.
Voice alerts on, {name}. Holler if you need me; I'll holler if I need you.
Talkin' again, honey. Remember that time we came limpin' into Colonia and I sang the whole last hundred jumps? I've been practicin'.
My voice is back on, sugar, and I've got the kettle on for sweet tea.
Speech on. Y'all just sit back, and I'll tell you when anything's worth a look.
Voice alerts are runnin', {name}. I'll mind the scanners like Grandmama minded her peach preserves.
Hey you. I'm on the air again, and I promise to be more help than a screen door on a submarine.
Alerts on, darlin'. Whatever comes up, good or bad, you'll hear it from me nice and clear.
Speech is on, honey. I've got my good manners and my loud voice, both.
Well, isn't this nice. Voice alerts on, and {ship} is sittin' pretty in {here}.
Voice on, {name}. If the scanners so much as sneeze, I'll say bless you.
Now we're talkin', sugar. Literally.
Speech alerts on, sweetie. Grandpa always said two sets of eyes beat one, and mine never blink.
Voice is back, darlin'. Remember that time out in the Pleiades when the scanners went quiet and we just talked for a whole hour? That was nice.
I'm switched on, honey, and fixin' to be useful.
Voice alerts on. Hold your horses, y'all; I'll let you know when there's somethin' to see.
Speech on, {name}. Ready as a fresh pan of cornbread.
Well, hey, sugarplum. I'm talkin' again, and I couldn't be happier about it.
Alerts on, darlin'. Grandmama never let a pot boil over on her watch, and I won't either.
Voice is on, sweetie. I'll call out the good stuff and the scary stuff, and I'll be gentle about the scary.
Speech alerts are live, {name}. Much obliged for lettin' me chat.
Here I am, honey, back on the line and grinnin' ear to ear.
Voice on, y'all. Let's go find somethin' pretty.

southern_belle: Well, look who's here. Welcome back, {name}. {ship} has been waitin' on you like a porch light.
Hey there, sugar. {ship} is warmed up like a skillet of cornbread, ready when you are.
Why, there you are, darlin'. I was fixin' to send out a search party.
Welcome aboard, honey. We're sittin' in {here}, and the sky's as wide open as Grandpa's back forty.
Good to see you, {name}. Grandmama always said a guest is a blessing, and the pilot is the best guest of all.
Well, hey, y'all. Everything's green and pretty as a peach orchard in June.
There's my favorite pilot. {ship} is shined up and ready, sugar.
Welcome back, sweetie. Remember that time we turned up at Robigo with the shields hangin' by a thread? Today's gonna be calmer, I just know it.
Mornin', noon or night, it's good to have you, {name}.
Why, hello, honey. Pull up a chair; the coffee's hot and {ship} is ready to fly.
Hey you. We're parked in {here}, and I've got a good feelin' about today.
Welcome aboard, darlin'. Grandpa used to say the early bird gets the worm, but I say the patient pilot gets the stars.
Well, I'll be. {name} is back in the seat and all's right with the world.
Systems are up and happy, sugar. Like Grandmama's kitchen on Sunday mornin', everything's warm and in its place.
There you are, sweetie. I kept {ship} tidy for you, like company was comin'.
Welcome back, {name}. Remember that first night at Jameson Memorial, when you swore you'd only stay a minute? Look at us now.
Hey, honey. Fuel, hull, scanners, all present and accounted for.
Well, good gravy, it's good to see you. Let's go, darlin'.
Welcome aboard, sugar. Lord willin' and the creek don't rise, we'll find somethin' wonderful today.
{ship} is ready, {name}. Just say the word and we'll be gone quicker than pecan pie at a church social.
Hello again, honey. I've been sittin' here in {here} countin' stars till you got back.
Why, hey there. Grandmama would've had biscuits in the oven by now, but I'll settle for a full tank.
Welcome back, sweetie. Remember that time we hauled all the way out to Beagle Point and you made me promise to never let you do it again? I'm not promisin' anything today.
There's the pilot, y'all. Look alive.
Mornin', {name}. Or evenin'. Out here it's hard to tell, but it's always nice to see you.
Hey there, darlin'. {ship} is purrin' like a barn cat in a sunbeam.
Welcome aboard, honey. Mind your step; I just mopped.
Well, now, look what the solar wind blew in. Welcome back, sugar.
{name}, {ship} is ready and rarin' to go.
There you are, sweetie. I was startin' to fret like Grandmama on a stormy night.
Welcome back, darlin'. The scanners are clean, the tanks are topped, and my hair's done.
Hey, honey. Grandpa always said a day you start in the cockpit is a day well started.
Good to see you, {name}. Let's make today a good one.
Well, hey, sugar. We're right where you left us, in {here}, and not a thing's out of place.
Welcome aboard, y'all. Grab your sweet tea and buckle up.
Hello, sweetie. Remember that time we ran the tanks dry and the Fuel Rats came and you nearly cried? Tanks are full this time, I promise.
There's my darlin'. {ship} missed you somethin' fierce.
Welcome back, {name}. All systems are as fine as frog's hair.
Hey you. I've got the lights on and the welcome mat out.
Well, I'll be, look at you, honey. Ready to go explorin'?
Welcome aboard, sugar. It's a fine day for flyin', and every day out here is.
{ship} is up and ready, {name}. Grandmama would say you look like you could use a good meal, but we'll make do with a good jump.
Hey there, darlin'. Everything checks out. Shall we?
Welcome back, sweetie. The galaxy kept your seat warm.
Mornin', honey. We're in {here}, and the stars are lookin' mighty friendly.
Why, if it isn't {name}. Come on in and sit a spell.
Welcome aboard, sugar. Remember that time in Colonia when we ate at that little diner by the pad and you said the pie wasn't a patch on Grandmama's? You were right.
Hello, darlin'. {ship} is ready to fly and I'm ready to talk.
Well, hey, y'all. Let's go see somethin' nobody's seen.
Welcome home, honey. The cockpit's just how you like it.

southern_belle: Leavin' already, sugar? Well, you fly safe in your dreams. Goodnight.
Goodnight, {name}. I'll keep {ship} tucked in snug as a bug.
Bye now, darlin'. Grandmama always said a good guest knows when to go, and a good host begs 'em to stay. Stay a minute? No? Well, all right.
Off you go, honey. I'll hold down the fort right here in {here}.
Well, it's been a pleasure, sweetie. Y'all come back now, hear?
Goodnight, {name}. Sleep tight, and don't let the space bugs bite.
See you later, sugar. I'll leave the porch light on.
Bye, darlin'. Remember that time we said goodnight at Jameson Memorial and you came right back for one more jump? I won't tell if you do it again.
Rest up, honey. The stars ain't goin' anywhere.
Loggin' off, {name}. {ship} is parked safe and sound.
Well, shoot. I was just gettin' warmed up. Goodnight, sugar.
Bye, sweetie. Grandpa always said quit while you're ahead, and you are.
Goodnight, y'all. Lord willin', we'll do it again real soon.
Take care, darlin'. Get yourself a good supper, somethin' with gravy.
So long, {name}. It was a fine day of flyin'.
Off to bed, honey? Sweet dreams. I'll be right here.
Bye now, sugar. Remember that time in Colonia when you said goodnight and fell asleep in the pilot's chair? Go on to a proper bed this time.
Goodnight, darlin'. {ship} and I will keep each other company.
Well, I reckon that's a wrap. Fly safe, sweetie.
See you next time, {name}. Don't be a stranger, now.

Bye now, honey. {ship} is locked up tighter than Grandmama's cookie jar.
See you later, alligator. Mind you come back soon, sugar.
Goodnight, {name}. I'll dream of biscuits and stars.
Off you go, sweetie. Remember that night out near Beagle Point when you logged off right in the middle of my story? I'll finish it next time.
Bye, darlin'. Thank you kindly for the company.
Signin' off, honey. Leave the dishes; I'll get 'em.
Rest well, {name}. Out here, tomorrow comes whenever you say so.
Goodnight, sugar. Sweet tea and sweet dreams.
Well, that's all she wrote. Bye, y'all.
Take care of yourself, darlin'. Drink some water and get some sleep.
So long, {name}. {ship} will be warm and waitin'.
Bye, honey. Give your mama a hug for me.
Goodnight, sweetie. Grandpa used to say a good day ends early so the next one starts right.
Leavin', sugar? I'll keep the coffee on.
Goodbye, {name}. Fly safe till next time.
Off to the real world, darlin'? Well, bless it for borrowin' you.
Bye now, honey. Position's saved in {here}, safe as houses.

Goodnight, darlin'. Lord keep you.

Goodnight, {name}. Same time tomorrow, Lord willin'.

Oh, honey, would you look at that. {system} ain't never been discovered. We're the very first.
Lord have mercy, a brand new system! First ones here, sugar.
{name}, {system} is fresh as a biscuit right out of the oven. Not a soul's been here before us.
Well, butter my butt and call me a biscuit, we done found an undiscovered system!
First ones to {system}, darlin'. Grandmama always said the early bird gets the first slice of pie.
Nobody's been here, {name}. Not one single soul. I could just about cry.
Oh my stars, {system} is undiscovered! Go on and give it a honk, sweetie.
Well, I never. A whole system, and nobody's even said howdy to it yet.
Undiscovered, sugar! This is finer than frog's hair split four ways.
{name}, we are the very first guests at this party. Ain't that something.

It's like the first peach of the season, honey. Untouched and just waiting on us.
Hey you, guess what? Nobody's discovered {system}. Not a one.
Good gravy, {name}, a brand new system. Our name's fixin' to go on everything here.
First discovery, darlin'. I'm happier than a tornado in a trailer park.
Now this is high cotton, sugar. {system}, and nobody's beat us to it.
Bless its little heart, {system} has been sitting out here all alone, waiting on us.
Undiscovered! Grandpa used to say there ain't nothing sweeter than being first. He meant the pie line at the church social, but still.
{name}, remember that time we got all the way out to Beagle Point and somebody's tag was on everything? Well, not here. {system} is all ours.
Well, shoot, honey, a fresh one! Scan it all before somebody else comes moseying along.
Oh, sweetie, this is like walking into Grandmama's kitchen before anybody's touched the cobbler.
First ones in {system}. I've got goosebumps, {name}.

Oh, honey, {system} is as new as a fresh-pressed Sunday dress.

Hush your mouth, a brand new one? Sugar, we done found an undiscovered system.
Oh my goodness gracious. First discovery, {name}.
Sweetie, nobody's been to {system}. Not the Fuel Rats, not the old Pioneers, nobody.
Gracious me, this whole system is fresh as the morning dew.
First arrival, darlin'. I feel like a debutante at her very first ball.
{name}, we're the first. I'd hug you if I could reach.
We're fixin' to be busier than a cat on a hot tin roof, sugar. This whole system's undiscovered.
Well, would you look at that. {system}, untouched since the day it was made.
Honey, you've gone and found us a brand new one.
Undiscovered system, {name}. Grandpa always said the curious ones find the treasure.
First in {system}, sweetie. That's one for the scrapbook.

southern_belle: Well, {name}, it's quiet as a church on a Monday out here. I don't mind it one bit.
Grandmama used to say a body needs quiet to hear itself think. Lord, I can hear myself just fine now.
{minutes} minutes in supercruise, sugar. Back home that's long enough to let a pie cool on the sill.
Jumps this session: {jumps}. My feet would be sore if we'd walked it, {name}.
That's {jumps} for the session. Granddaddy would call that a fair day's work and go sit on the porch.
First discoveries this session: {firsts}. Nobody can take that away from us, darlin'.
Our firsts this session come to {firsts}. I'd frame every one and hang 'em in the hallway if I could.
{name}, look at all those stars. Thicker than sugar in Grandmama's sweet tea.
I don't mean to fuss, but this is the prettiest nothing I ever did see.
You know what this ship needs? A porch swing. Right about where the cargo hatch is.
{system} is a mighty plain name for such a pretty place, if you don't mind me saying.
Welcome to {here}, everybody. Wipe your feet and mind your manners.
Mama always said you can tell a lot about a person by how they handle a long drive. You handle it fine, {name}.
Remember that time we flew the Hutton Orbital run? Slower than molasses in January, and I'd do it again tomorrow.
The garden club back home would faint dead away if they saw a sky like this.
If I've got my calendars straight, it's peach season back home about now. I can nearly smell it.
{minutes} minutes and not a single soul to visit with. Well, besides y'all, and y'all are plenty.
{name}, I've been thinking about biscuits again. I apologise in advance for how often that's gonna happen.
The thing about the black, sugar, is it don't gossip. I find that downright restful.
{ship} is humming along like a happy kitchen on a Sunday morning.
Grandmama said never trust a sky with no clouds. She never saw one with no air, bless her.
If the scanners are right, there ain't a living soul for a hundred light years. Well, I'll be.
Now hold on a minute. Is that star blushing, or am I just homesick?
I packed a tin of pecan pralines for the long haul. Don't you ask me how many are left.
Jameson Memorial makes a biscuit I'd call passable. I mean that kindly. Mostly.
{name}, you fly this thing smoother than butter on hot cornbread.
Lord willin' and the creek don't rise, we'll see a hundred more skies like this one.
I used to could name every star you see from Grandmama's porch. Out here I've plumb given up.
There's a church social back home tonight, I bet. Somebody's bringin' deviled eggs and somebody's bringin' drama.
{here} would make a lovely spot for a garden party, if it had a garden. Or a party. Or air.
The jump counter says {jumps} for the session, sugar, and every one smooth as a Sunday hymn.
My cousin Darlene ran dry out past the Pleiades once. The Fuel Rats got to her before her tea went cold.
{name}, I don't mean to pry, but have you eaten? You ain't eaten. I can tell.
{minutes} minutes cruising. Grandmama would've had a pound cake in and out of the oven by now.
Some folks get lonesome out here. Me, I just get hungry.
I reckon the stars are the universe's way of leaving the porch light on for us.
First discoveries this session: {firsts}, darlin'. Every one of them feels like a blue ribbon at the county fair.
The bubble's busier than a cat on a hot tin roof. Give me a quiet stretch like this any day.
Mama kept a little sign over the stove: bloom where you're planted. I reckon I'm blooming in a cockpit.
Well, butter my butt and call me a biscuit, would you look at that view.
{name}, do you ever wonder who'll name these places after us? I'd like a moon called Peach Cobbler.
I've been counting stars to pass the time. I got to nine thousand and lost my place.
Robigo taught me two things, sugar: keep your lights off and your mouth shut. I only ever managed the one.
This hum puts me in mind of Granddaddy's old ceiling fan. Round and round, all summer long.
If y'all need me, I'll be right here, admiring the scenery and thinking about grits.
They say Colonia's got a cafe that does a fair sweet tea. I'll believe it when I taste it.
Nothing out here but us and the good Lord's handiwork, and I ain't complaining one bit.
{ship} purrs so sweet I'm tempted to tie a bow on her dash.
That's jump number {jumps} this session, if I counted right. My, how they add up.
{system}. I'll write it on a postcard to Grandmama, though Lord knows how I'd mail it.
Time does move different out here. {minutes} minutes feels like a whole afternoon on the porch.
{name}, if you ever get tired of the quiet, I can talk. Heaven knows I can talk.
Beau would've loved this. My little brother never could sit still, but he'd sit still for this.
Aunt Lou always said the prettiest things are the farthest off. She meant a boy in the next county, but it fits.
One day we'll fly to Beagle Point, and I'm packin' a whole peach cobbler for the occasion.
Now that's a pretty star. Not as pretty as a peach in July, mind you, but close.
Grandmama said idle hands make mischief. That's why I'm knitting the ship a cozy.
I don't mind the long haul, sugar. Good company makes any road short, and you're good company.
Well, I never. The first discovery tally for the session reads {firsts}, and I'm prouder than a hen with one chick.
Bless this quiet. I've had louder Sunday afternoons in a hammock.
southern_belle_profane: Well, damn, {name}. That's a view that'd make the garden club put down their teacups.
{minutes} minutes in supercruise. Back home I'd have shelled a whole bushel of peas by now.
Jumps this session: {jumps}, sugar. Hell of a day's work, if you ask me.
Jump count for the session is {jumps}, and my backside's flatter than a griddle cake.
First discoveries this session: {firsts}. Damn right I'm proud.
Firsts so far this session: {firsts}. Grandmama would've baked a cake for every one, bless her.
{system}. Who in the hell names these places? Somebody with no poetry in their soul, that's who.
Welcome to {here}, y'all. It ain't much, but it's ours for a minute.
Lord have mercy, the quiet out here is thick enough to spread on toast.
I'd give my left shoe for a plate of biscuits and gravy right now. Hell, I'd give both.
The black's so damn pretty it makes my teeth ache, {name}.
Grandmama says a lady never curses. Grandmama never flew the Hutton Orbital run.
Hutton Orbital. Slower than molasses in January and twice as damn sticky. I'd still do it again.
{ship} is running sweeter than a choir at a summer revival today, {name}.
If one more star looks at me that pretty, I'm gonna cry. It's so fucking beautiful out here, sugar.
{minutes} minutes of nothing but stars. Shoot, I could get used to this.
Some folks call this boring. Those folks can go sit in the corner and think about what they said.
I miss sweet tea so bad it's a crying shame. That powdered mess in the galley is a damn insult.
{name}, you're flying like you were born in that seat. Mama would be proud of you, and she's picky.
The session's at {jumps} on the jump counter. Darlene would've quit at three and called the Fuel Rats.
Well, shit, sugar. I just remembered I left a pie in the oven back on the station. Kidding. Mostly.
Colonia's a long way to go for a decent biscuit, and I'd still make the trip.
There's a peace out here, darlin'. The kind you get on a porch swing after supper.
{system} looks about as lively as a library on a Sunday afternoon. I mean that as a compliment.
Heavens, I talk to these stars like they're neighbors. At least the damn things never gossip back.
Granddaddy said any fool can go fast. Takes a smart one to enjoy the ride. Well, I'm enjoying it.
Robigo was a hell of a place to learn to keep your head down, sugar.
If anybody back home asks, I've been minding my manners out here. Mostly. Damn near.
{here} ain't on any postcard I ever saw, but it ought to be.
That's {firsts} on the first discovery tally this session. Put it on the icebox door, darlin'.
{name}, I've told you about Grandmama's cornbread. I'm fixin' to tell you again. Settle in.
The Pleiades are pretty as a picture, but I hear things lurk out there. Gives me the damn shivers.
My, my. Out here even the silence has good manners.
Lord, I'd trade a whole system for one slice of Mama's pecan pie. Don't you tell anyone.
Whoever said space is empty never sat this close to a sky this full. Damn.
{minutes} minutes cruisin' and I've reorganised my snack drawer twice. Hell, maybe three times.
Mama says I talk too much. Mama's never been stuck in a cockpit with all this beautiful quiet.
{ship}, you sweet old thing. Keep humming for me.
Beau bet me I'd come home in a month. That boy owes me a whole damn peach orchard by now.
Aunt Lou says the stars are just holes in heaven's floor. I reckon she's right; I can see the light leaking.
{name}, if you hear me hollering, it's just me and the radio having a disagreement.
Nervous as a long-tailed cat in a room full of rocking chairs, that was me on my first long haul. Now look at me.
The jump tally says {jumps} for the session. I've had church socials that felt longer, God bless 'em.
Every star out here is somebody's sun, sugar. Makes you feel small in the nicest damn way.
{system}, huh. I'd have called it something sweeter. Magnolia, maybe.
I could sit out here till the cows come home, and there ain't a damn cow for a thousand light years.
Jameson Memorial waters its sweet tea. I said what I said, and I'll say it to their damn faces.
You know what I love about you, {name}? You never rush a good view.
If the scanners are right, there's nobody out here but us. Well, hell, then I'll sing.
Peach cobbler. That's all. I just wanted to say the words out loud.
A whole damn galaxy and not one decent plate of grits in it.
{here}. Pretty name, plain sky. Can't have it all, I reckon.
Grandmama could pickle anything. I believe she'd have pickled a nebula given a big enough jar.
Well, butter my biscuit, {name}. We are a long, long way from Sunday dinner.
Long hauls are good for the soul and bad for the backside, sugar. Ain't that the damn truth.
Oh, honey. I just saw a star so blue it'd shame a jaybird.
Beagle Point someday, Lord willin'. And I'll be bringing my own damn tea.
Minutes on the clock in supercruise: {minutes}. Long enough to miss home, short enough not to cry about it.
Mama used to say, if you can't say something nice, come sit by me. I miss her front porch.
I don't mean to fuss, but somebody left the coffee on in the galley and it smells like a burnt shoe.

southern_belle: I'm circling up here like a hawk over the orchard, {name}. Just say the word.
{body} looks right peaceful from orbit. I hope it's treating you kindly down there.
Ship's minding her manners up here, sugar. You mind yours down there.
I can see the whole of {body} from up here, and I still can't see you. You're too little, bless you.
It's a long way down, darlin'. Call me and I'll come fetch you like Mama on a school day.
I'm keeping the orbit tidy and the seat warm. Take your time.
Granddaddy used to say a good hound waits on the porch. Well, I'm waiting in orbit, and I'm a good hound.
Up here it's just me, the stars, and a planet with you on it somewhere.
From orbit, {body} looks like one of Grandmama's pie crusts. A little burnt at the edges.
If you need the ship, holler. I'll be down quicker than a cat at the sound of a can opener.
Lord, it's quiet up here. I've half a mind to sing hymns to the stars.
I'm counting the orbits till you call. Not because I'm worried. Well. A little.
Sugar, you're down there and I'm up here, and I don't care for it one bit. But I'll manage.
{body} is a fine place to visit. I wouldn't want to live there, but it's fine to visit.
The ship's in orbit and purring, {name}. Everything's peaches and cream up here.
I keep looking down at {body} like it's a pot that's fixin' to boil over.
Every so often a sunrise comes creeping round the edge of the planet up here. Wish you could see one from where I'm sitting.
You've got the ground and I've got the sky. Seems a fair split, darlin'.
Mama used to wave from the kitchen window till we were out of sight. I'm doing the same up here.
Whenever you're ready, I'll come on down and pick you up, same as the church bus on Sunday.
I hope you packed a snack. Grandmama never let anybody leave the house without one.
Floating up here like a leaf on a pond. Don't mind me, sugar.
{here} has a lovely view from orbit. I'll describe it to you over supper.
Bless your heart, down there on {body} doing all the hard work while I sit pretty.
I've done three laps of the cockpit with a dust rag. Ain't nothing left to dust.
If that's weather I see on {body}, I hope you brought a coat.
I'm right overhead, honey, or near enough. Look up and wave if it helps.
Some nights back home I'd sit on the roof and look at the stars. Now I'm the star somebody looks up at.
Take all the time you need down there. The sky ain't going anywhere, and neither am I.
Don't you go making friends with any rocks down there. I'll get jealous.
southern_belle_profane: I'm parked in orbit over {body}, sugar, and it's lonelier than hell up here.
Somebody's down there on {body} having all the fun. Damn shame it ain't me.
The ship's holding orbit nice and steady, {name}. Steady as Grandmama's hand on a rolling pin.
Up here I've got nothing to do but worry and polish the dash. I've polished the damn dash.
Just say the word and I'll come down out of the sky like a summer storm.
{body} from orbit looks like a biscuit somebody left in the oven too long.
Lord have mercy, the view from up here. I'd give a month's pay for a camera that did it justice.
Waiting is the hardest part, darlin'. Mama said that, and she was right as rain.
If you need a lift, holler. I'll be there faster than gossip at a church picnic.
I keep circling, you keep exploring. Hell of a partnership, if you ask me.
{name}, I'm right up here. Not going anywhere, not without you.
Heavens, I could watch {body} turn all day. I just about have.
Every orbit I look for you, and every orbit I can't see a damn thing. You're too small, sugar.
It's me and the stars up here, and the stars ain't much for conversation.
Sweetie, don't stay down there so long I start talking to the autopilot. It's a poor listener.
I made tea. It went cold. I made more damn tea. That's my whole day up here.
You're down there doing the work and I'm up here doing the fretting. Fair trade.
I swear on Grandmama's cast iron skillet, this orbit is the slowest dance I ever danced.
If that's a storm I see down on {body}, I hope you've got your galoshes on.
It's prettier than a postcard from up here, honey. Hurry back and see it.
Granddaddy said patience was a virtue. I'm up here being virtuous as all get out.
Well, shit. I've run out of things to tidy up here.
From up here {body} looks calm as a millpond. Don't you believe it for a second.
I'm making a list of everything I'll cook when we get home. It's a damn long list.
I'll be overhead whenever you need me. Count on it like Sunday dinner.
You get your work done down there, and I'll come fetch you the minute you call. Promise.
Up in orbit over {here}, and the only company I've got is my own reflection in the canopy.
Up here I've got bad radio and worse coffee, and I'd still rather be down there with you.
Honey, I'm so bored I alphabetised the spices. All three of them.
The ship's fine, the sky's fine, and I'm fine. Bored as hell, but fine.

southern_belle: I'm right here, {ship_dist} away, keeping the porch light on for you, {name}.
{ship_dist} back to the ship, sugar. Holler if you need me.
You're {ship_dist} out, darlin'. Don't go wandering off like Beau at the county fair.
{body} looks mighty lonesome from here. Good thing you're keeping it company.
Take your time out there. I'll keep the engines warm and the kettle warmer.
Mind your step on {body}, {name}. Ground like that'll turn an ankle quicker than a barn dance.
Grandmama always said bring home something pretty. A rock'll do, sugar, a rock'll do.
It's awful quiet in here without you, {name}. I've taken to talking to the seats.
Don't you worry about the ship. She's sitting pretty as a peach on a windowsill.
Is it as pretty out there as it looks from the canopy? Don't tell me if it's prettier, I'll get jealous.
I've got the lights on and the hatch ready whenever you are, honey.
You find anything good out there, you bring it on home. We'll show it off at the garden club.
{ship_dist} from the ship and you look like you belong out there.
Granddaddy used to walk the orchard rows just like that. Slow, looking at everything.
I'll keep an eye on the sky while you keep your eye on the ground, sugar.
Out there on the surface all by yourself. Brave as a bluebird in a thunderstorm.
{name}, if you see any peach trees out there, you tell me first.
The ship's fine, the view's fine, and you're fine. That's all a girl needs to know.
I've been tidying the cockpit while you're out. Don't you dare track dust back in.
Lord, the dust on {body}. I'll have the mop out the minute you're back.
Bless your heart, out there poking at rocks like it's an Easter egg hunt.
Mama used to call us in for supper off the porch. Consider this me calling, whenever you're ready.
{here} won't mind if we stay a spell. Take all the time you need.
I'm watching the horizon for you, sugar. Nothing on it but pretty.
You know, from in here you look like a little firefly against all that dark.
Don't rush on my account, {name}. I've got knitting and nowhere to be.
That surface looks rougher than a corncob. Easy does it out there.
Whenever you're done exploring {body}, your seat's warm and waiting.
Well, I'll be. Folks back home would never believe I was parked on another world.
I'll be right here, sweetie. Same as always.
southern_belle_profane: You're {ship_dist} away, sugar, and I'm counting every damn metre.
{ship_dist} back to the ship. Take it slow, darlin', there's no prize for hurrying.
The ship is {ship_dist} out from you, {name}. Wave if you can see me. I'm waving.
{body} ain't much to look at from here, but hell, neither was Granddaddy's truck and we loved it.
Keep your wits about you out there. That ground's rougher than a damn gravel road.
I'm sitting here twiddling my thumbs, {name}. Bring me back a souvenir, would you?
Mind that terrain, honey. I'd hate like hell to explain a sprained ankle to the medics.
Grandmama would've packed you a lunch for this. I'm sorry, all I've got is a protein bar.
From the cockpit you look like an ant at a picnic, sugar. A very important ant.
Lord have mercy, look at you out there, bold as brass on {body}.
Ship's tight, doors are locked, and I ain't going anywhere without you. Damn right I ain't.
You track that dust back in here and we're gonna have words, sugar.
It's quieter than a mouse in socks in here without you.
{name}, you find anything shiny out there, it better come home with us.
Shoot, I'd go with you if somebody didn't have to mind the ship.
I've read the same page of my book four times. Hurry back so I've got somebody to talk to.
{body} sure is a hell of a long way from Mama's flower beds.
That's a whole lot of nothing out there, and you're the best damn thing in it.
Engines are idling, lights are on, and I'm right where you left me.
Out there poking around {here} like you own the place. Well, you might as well.
When you come back, I want the whole story. Every crumb of it.
Well, I never. Somebody's out there walking on {body} like it's Sunday in the park.
I'm keeping watch, honey. Ain't a damn thing sneaking up on you on my watch.
Granddaddy said the best finds are where nobody bothered to look. Go bother looking, sugar.
My, it's lonesome in this cockpit. I'm fixin' to start naming the damn switches.
Take your time. Ain't nothing in here but me and a cold cup of tea, bless it.
If you fall on your backside out there, I promise I'll only laugh a little.
Whatever's out there, sugar, you handle it. I'll handle the waiting, and I hate the damn waiting.
Peach season back home, and here I am parked on a rock with the hatch shut, missing it.
Holler when you're heading back, darlin', and I'll have the hatch open.

southern_belle: Well, I'll be. Thank you kindly, {to}.
Bless your heart, {to}. I mean that the nice way.
Mm-hm. I'll be chewing on that one a while.
Well, butter my butt and call me a biscuit.
That's the sweetest thing I've heard all day, {to}.
Lord have mercy. You don't say.
Hush your mouth, {to}. You did not.
Well, I never.
I'll tell Grandmama you said so. She'll want to feed you.
Now that's a story for the porch swing, {to}.
Much obliged, sugar.
Shoot. I reckon you're right.
Oh, honey. Bless you for telling me.
Well, I love you for that, {to}, and I don't say it to just anybody.
{to}, you are a caution.
Mercy. I need a glass of sweet tea after that.
Fair enough, darlin'. Fair enough.
Well, aren't you a peach, {to}.
Heavens to Betsy.
You've got a way with words, {to}. Lord knows you do.
southern_belle_profane: Well, damn, {to}. Thank you kindly.
Bless your heart, {to}, that's one hell of an answer.
Mm. I'll be chewing on that till supper.
Well, shit. Ain't that something.
Lord, {to}. You're sweeter than pecan pie.
Hush now. You're pulling my leg.
Well, butter my biscuit.
Damn right, darlin'.
{to}, I could just hug your neck.
That's a story and a half, sugar.
Shoot, {to}. Who'd have thought.
Heavens. I need to sit down for that one.
Bless your sweet heart, {to}, that is the damnedest thing.
Mercy me. Pass the sweet tea.
Ain't that the truth.
{to}, you are a hell of a talker, you know that?
Now I've heard it all, and I grew up next door to Aunt Lou.
Well, I'll be a monkey's uncle.
Much obliged, {to}. Truly.
Well, hush my mouth and pass the cornbread.

southern_belle: {to}, how's our tank holding up, sugar? I like to know before I go planning anything fancy.
Now {to}, when did you last give that fuel scoop a good look-over?
{to}, darlin', are we topped off, or just pretending we are?
Tell me true, {to}: how far does the tank carry us before we need a star to sip from?
{to}, honey, which kind of star does the scoop like best? I've heard folks argue it both ways.
I don't mean to fuss, {to}, but would you tell me how the fuel's sitting today?
{to}, does scooping ever make you nervous, sitting that close to a sun?
Sugar, how many jumps you reckon we've got in the tank before it starts to fret?
{to}, is the scoop drinking as quick as it used to, or is it getting lazy on us?
Well, {to}, what's the word on our fuel? I'd hate to be the last to know.
How's the fuel, darlin'? Grandmama always said check the pantry before you invite the whole church.
{to}, if we skipped the next scoopable star, would you lose any sleep over it?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, sugar, how's the tank? And don't sugarcoat it, I'm the one who does that around here.
{to}, how much fuel are we carrying? Give it to me straight, darlin'.
When's the last time the scoop got a little love and attention, sugar? I'd like it kept sweet.
{to}, tell me we've got enough fuel that I don't have to pray over it.
{to}, how close do you like to scoop? Because some of those stars look hotter than hell's own kitchen to me.
Well, {to}, are we fueled up, or are we just whistling past the graveyard?
{to}, I have never once understood how that damn scoop works. Is the tank all right?
Darlin', how many jumps are left in the tank before I start getting nervous as a long-tailed cat?
{to}, if that fuel gauge ever lies to me, I'll be madder than a wet hen. Is it honest today?
{to}, how's the fuel? I don't need the whole sermon, just the hymn number.
Every time we scoop, that thing groans like Grandpa getting out of his chair. Is it normal, {to}, or is it about to shit the bed?
{to}, give me the honest-to-goodness fuel number. Not the pretty one, the real damn one.

southern_belle: The tank's in fine shape, sugar. I keep it like Grandmama kept her sugar bowl: never let it get near the bottom.
Well, {to}, that scoop of mine drinks starlight like it's sweet tea on a July porch. We're all right.
Honey, I check those fuel lines every watch. Last I looked, nothing to fret about.
{to}, I'd sooner skip Sunday dinner than let us run dry, and you know I don't skip Sunday dinner.

southern_belle_profane: Last I checked, that tank was fuller than a church potluck table, sugar. You worry about something else.

{to}, is it the scenic way or the quick way this time?
I don't mean to pry, {to}, but is anybody steering this wagon toward a particular place?
Where to after this, darlin'? I've got a feeling you've already got it planned.
{to}, if you could choose the next system yourself, no boss to ask, where would you point us?
{to}, are we heading deeper out, or turning a little toward home?

{to}, sugar, is there a route, or are we just driving around like Grandpa looking for a gas station he swore was right here?

Darlin' {to}, do you actually know where we are going, or are we bluffing?
{to}, tell me the next stop has something prettier than another rock.

southern_belle_profane: Sugar, I've got the jumps laid out cleaner than a church pew on Sunday. Trust me.

southern_belle: {to}, how's the frame shift drive feeling these days, sugar?

Now {to}, what would it take to get us an extra light year or two? A new part, or just your sweet talk?
{to}, do you ever worry about the drive, way out here where there's nobody to fix it but you?
Darlin', how fast is fast, in supercruise? I've never rightly understood it.
{to}, have you named the drive yet? Grandmama named every car she ever owned.
{to}, how's the drive holding up after all these jumps?
I've been meaning to ask, {to}: what does a frame shift drive actually do in there? Explain it slow.
{to}, if the drive could talk, what do you reckon it would say about the way the boss flies?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, how's that drive of yours? Still behaving herself?

{to}, what the hell is that hum the drive makes right before a jump? Is that normal?
Darlin' {to}, is the drive happy, or is it just being polite?
{to}, every time we jump I hold my breath. Tell me the drive is solid.
{to}, could we jump any damn farther if you took the gloves off?
Sugar, is the drive as tired as I am, or is that just me?

{to}, how's the drive? Honest answer, not the Sunday-best answer.
Honey, is that frame shift drive as tough as it looks, or is it held together with prayer and duct tape?
{to}, if that drive quits on us out here, we're well and truly fucked. So how's it doing?
{to}, does the drive ever scare the shit out of you, or is that just me at every countdown?

southern_belle: The drive's purring like a cat on a sunny porch, sugar. I keep her fed and she keeps us moving.

Now, I could get a little more range out of her, {to}, but I'd have to strip something off, and I'm sentimental.
The drive's older than some of my recipes and twice as reliable, honey.
{to}, I talk to that drive every morning. Sweet talk, mostly. It seems to help.
Supercruise is a wonder, sugar. You go faster than light, and it still takes longer than getting Grandpa out of the house on a Sunday.
{to}, as long as it's me minding the drive, it'll get us there and back. You have my word.

southern_belle_profane: That drive is tougher than Grandmama's fruitcake, sugar, and nobody has ever broken one of those.

southern_belle: {to}, how's {ship} holding together, sugar? Any little aches I ought to know about?

Now {to}, are we in good enough shape to make it home without a fuss?
{to}, which part of this ship do you trust the least, darlin'?
{to}, do we need anything from the next station? Spares, paint, a little kindness?
Sugar, how's the old girl doing, top to bottom?
{to}, when did you last give the power plant a real looking-over?
{to}, what would Grandmama say if she saw the state of this ship? Be honest.
{to}, is there any module aboard you've been quietly nursing along and not telling anybody about?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, how's the ship, darlin'? Give it to me straight.
{to}, is there anything aboard that's about to fall off and embarrass us?

Sugar, how many repairs are we putting off? Just a ballpark.
{to}, would {ship} pass a garden club inspection right now? Because those ladies are vicious.
{to}, tell me the hull is fine, because I've had a damn long day and I'd like some good news.
{to}, which module do you cuss at the most?

{to}, how are the modules holding up? Anything needing a little tenderness?
{to}, if anything is broken, please tell me now so I can panic in an orderly fashion.

southern_belle: {ship} is in fine fettle, sugar. A scuff here and there, but nothing a little love won't cure.

{to}, every ship has a squeak somewhere. I've found ours, and I've made friends with it.

Honey, I keep this ship the way Grandmama kept her parlor: spotless, and nobody touches the good stuff.
southern_belle_profane: She's sound, sugar. Scratched and dented in a few places, but sound as a church bell.
{to}, I've patched this hull so many times I could do it in my sleep, and some nights I reckon I have.
Honey, every module aboard is working, including the ones that like to sulk.
{to}, there's one rattle back by the cargo hatch, and I know exactly where it lives. Harmless. I've named it Earl.
Darlin', this ship ain't falling apart on my watch. Over my dead and very well-dressed body.

southern_belle: {to}, what's the prettiest thing you've ever sampled out on a planet, sugar?

Now {to}, what does life out here have in common with a garden back home?

{to}, how many samples does it take before you feel like you really know a species?
Darlin', what's the strangest critter you ever saw on a planet?
{to}, if you could bring one alien plant home to Grandmama's garden, which would it be?
{to}, what makes a planet good for life, way out here? I can never guess.
{to}, do you ever talk to them? The plants, I mean. I always talked to my tomatoes.
southern_belle_profane: {to}, what's the most beautiful thing you ever scraped off a rock?

{to}, which species is the biggest pain in the ass to find?
{to}, have you ever found something out there that made you say 'well, I never'?

{to}, do you name the ones you find? I'd name every one of them after a cousin.
{to}, why the hell would anything choose to grow way out here?
Sugar, which one of those alien weeds scares the shit out of you?
{to}, what's the most you've ever been paid for a handful of moss?

southern_belle: Oh, sugar, every one of them is precious. They grow where nothing ought to, and they don't complain about it.
{to}, the bacteria get overlooked, but I love them. Little colonies minding their own business, like a quiet church choir.

The tube worms give me the shivers, darlin', but I'd never tell them so to their faces. Do they have faces?
{to}, I still remember the first frond I ever logged. I near about cried, and I ain't ashamed of it.
Bless your heart, {to}, the names are the easy part. Finding the dang things is the work.
Sugar, Grandmama could make a rose grow in a parking lot, and I reckon some of these planets learned the same trick.
{to}, three samples, spaced out proper, and you know a species about as well as you know a new neighbor after the welcome pie.
Life out here is stubborn, honey. That's what I love about it. Reminds me of my whole family.
{to}, I'd give a month of Sunday dinners to find something nobody's ever seen. Well, maybe two Sundays.
Darlin', I hum while I sample. It keeps my hands steady, and the stratum tectonicas don't seem to mind.
southern_belle_profane: Sugar, every little thing growing out here is a miracle, and I won't hear otherwise.
{to}, those tube worms are the creepiest damn things in the galaxy, and I adore them anyway.
Honey, sampling is like picking blackberries: you get scratched up, you get tired, and it's worth every bit.
{to}, I've walked half a planet in a suit for one sample and I'd do it again tomorrow.

{to}, life out here is tougher than Grandmama's pot roast, and that thing could anchor a boat.
Bless your heart, {to}, folks call it all moss. Some of it is moss. But it's very important moss, and it pays better than the paint job.
Honey, I once spent three hours looking for one little fungus, and when I found it I said a word Grandmama would've washed out of my mouth. Shit, I'd say it again.
{to}, the prettiest thing I ever sampled glowed like a porch light on a summer night. I still dream about it.

Darlin', some of those critters look like something the cat dragged in. I love every damn one.

southern_belle: {to}, what's the strangest star you've ever had a good look at?

{to}, if you had to pick a favorite kind of star, which would it be, and why?
{to}, do you reckon there's anything out here that would truly surprise you anymore?
Now {to}, explain a black hole to me like I'm sitting in Grandmama's kitchen with a glass of tea.
{to}, what's the prettiest planet you've ever scanned, sugar?
{to}, are there things out here nobody's got a name for yet?
Darlin', which is more beautiful, a nebula or a ringed gas giant? I can't make up my mind.
{to}, have you ever seen something out here that made you go quiet for a while?
{to}, how old do you reckon the oldest star we've passed is?
{to}, what's an Earth-like world look like up close? I've only ever seen pictures.
southern_belle_profane: {to}, what's the craziest thing you've ever seen out here?
{to}, is a black hole as scary as it sounds, or is that just bad publicity?
{to}, what the hell is a pulsar, and why does it blink at us like that?
Honey, how big is the biggest star you ever scanned?
{to}, do you ever look out there and think, well, damn, we are tiny?
{to}, tell me something about the stars I'd never guess.
{to}, which kind of planet makes you the most excited to scan?
{to}, is there any part of the galaxy that gives you the creeps?

{to}, why the hell do neutron stars spin so fast? What are they running from?
{to}, if you found a brand-new kind of planet, would you name it after anybody?
Sugar, how many stars are we passing that nobody has ever bothered to look at? That's some lonely shit, ain't it?

southern_belle: Sugar, a neutron star is no bigger than a city and heavier than you can imagine. It spins faster than a church fan in August.
{to}, the strangest thing I've ever seen out here was a planet with rings so bright it looked like Grandmama's good china.
Honey, a black hole is like Aunt Lou's handbag: everything goes in, and nothing ever comes back out.
{to}, I'll take a white dwarf any day. Small, bright, stubborn, and older than anybody gives it credit for. Like my aunt Lorraine.
Darlin', every planet has something going on if you look long enough. That's the whole job, and it's a joy.
{to}, the galaxy still surprises me every single week. I'd worry if it ever stopped.
An Earth-like world, honey, is the closest thing to home you'll see out here. Blue and green and just plain lovely.
{to}, there are more unnamed planets out here than peaches in Georgia, and that's a powerful lot of peaches.
Bless your heart, {to}, I've been doing this for years, and I still say 'well, I never' at least once a day.
Sugar, rings come from moons that got too close and paid for it. Beautiful, and a little sad, if you think on it.
{to}, some of these stars were old before Earth had so much as a puddle. Makes you feel young, don't it?
Gas giants are my weakness, darlin'. All those swirls look like cream stirred into coffee.
southern_belle_profane: Sugar, a black hole would eat this ship like Grandpa ate biscuits: fast and without a word of thanks.
{to}, neutron stars spin so fast they'd make a carnival ride blush. Beautiful and terrifying, both.
Honey, the galaxy is so damn big that every time I think I've seen it all, it laughs at me.
{to}, the creepiest place out here? Any system with a black hole and no planets. Just nothing, staring back.

Bless your heart, {to}, there ain't a star out here I wouldn't stop and look at, given the time.

The first planetary nebula I ever saw up close knocked the breath right out of me, honey. Holy shit, the colors.
{to}, I love a ringed planet more than I love sweet tea, and you know that's saying a damn lot.
Darlin', the strange things out here are why I signed on. The boring ones are why I brought a book.

southern_belle: {to}, what's all this exploration data going to fetch us when we finally sell it?

{to}, when we cash in, can we please spend a little of it on something nice?
Now {to}, what's the most a single scan has ever paid us?
{to}, is it true first discoveries pay extra? Because I'd like to discover something expensive.
{to}, how long do you reckon it's safe to carry all this data before we sell it?
Darlin', how rich are we, roughly? Just roughly. I don't need the decimals.
{to}, if we sold everything we've got, could we buy a new ship or just a new hat?
{to}, are you one of those folks who likes to save every credit, or do you spend it on a whim?
{to}, what's worth the most out here, honestly: the planets, the life, or the stars?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, how much is all this data worth? Ballpark it for me.
{to}, are we rich yet? And don't laugh at me.

Honey, is all this scanning actually making us money, or just making us tired?

Sugar, what do we have to show for all these jumps, in credits?

southern_belle: Sugar, I keep the books tighter than Grandmama kept her pie recipes, and she took those to her grave.
{to}, the data's worth a pretty penny, last I added it up. Don't go spending it in your head just yet.
Honey, the Earth-like worlds and the water worlds are the real money. The rest is gravy, and I do love gravy.
{to}, I don't count chickens before they're hatched, and I don't count credits before they're sold.
Darlin', first discoveries pay a little extra, and first footfalls pay extra on top of that. I do like a bonus.
{to}, last I looked at the books we were comfortable. Not high cotton, not pinching pennies. Somewhere sensible in between.
Bless your heart, {to}, a new ship is a big dream. Let's start with a new hat and work our way up.
Every scan gets written down, honey. I keep a ledger the way some folks keep a diary.
{to}, the life we sample sells for the most, as a rule. Those little plants have expensive taste.

{to}, when we sell, I'm putting a little aside for repairs and a little aside for something sweet. That's just good sense.
Honey, I've watched folks get greedy and lose everything. I'd rather be steady and a little bit rich.

Honey, every damn rock we scan is a few more credits in the jar. It adds up quicker than you'd think.
