{to}, I didn't come out here to scrape by. I came out here to come home in high cotton, and we damn well will.
Darlin', counting credits is the most peaceful part of my day. The rest of it is listening to y'all bicker.

southern_belle: {to}, do you miss the rings when we're out here doing nothing but scanning?
{to}, what's the best haul you ever pulled out of a ring, sugar?
Honey, is mining as much fun as it looks, or is it all hard work and rock dust?
{to}, which ore do you most love to find?
{to}, how do you know where to dig? Is it the scanner, or just a feeling in your bones?
Now {to}, could we fit a mining rig aboard without upsetting everything else?
{to}, have you ever cracked an asteroid open and just sat there admiring it?
{to}, what's the trick to a good mining run? Tell me like I've never done it.
Darlin', does all that laser work ever give you a headache?
{to}, if we found a pristine ring out here, would you be able to keep your hands off it?
{to}, is there anything prettier than a fresh-split chunk of painite?
{to}, did anybody in your family dig for a living, or did you come by it on your own?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, how bad do you miss mining, way out here?
{to}, what's the most money you ever pulled out of one rock?
{to}, is mining as boring as it looks, or is it worse?
Honey, do the rings ever scare you? All those rocks tumbling around?
{to}, tell me about the biggest damn rock you ever cracked.
{to}, would you trade your good boots for a mining laser? Asking for the boss.
{to}, what the hell is so special about painite anyway?
{to}, could we squeeze in a little mining on the way home, or is that crazy talk?
Darlin', how do you sit in a ring all day without losing your mind?
{to}, have you ever lost a whole haul? Lord, I'd be fit to be tied.
{to}, is it true you can blow an asteroid to bits? Because that sounds like a hell of a good time.
{to}, what's the worst thing about mining? And don't say the dust, I know about the damn dust.

southern_belle: Sugar, I miss the rings like I miss peach season. I know it'll come around again, and I'll be ready.
{to}, the best haul I ever pulled was a run of low temperature diamonds so pretty I almost didn't sell them.
Honey, mining is like shelling peas on Grandmama's porch: slow, steady, and it gets to be a meditation.
{to}, the trick is patience. You prospect, you pick your rock, and you don't get greedy.
Darlin', I'd take painite over any jewelry in a store. It's got character.
{to}, I'd find room for a rig. I'd find room if I had to sleep in the cargo hold myself.
A pristine ring out here? Lord have mercy, honey, you'd have to tie me to my chair.
{to}, cracking a core asteroid is the closest thing to fireworks on the Fourth I've found out here.
Bless your heart, {to}, it's half the scanner and half a feeling. Grandpa could find water with a stick, and I reckon I got the same knack for ore.
Sugar, rock dust gets everywhere, but so does flour in a good kitchen. A little mess means the work's getting done.
{to}, there's nothing so peaceful as a ring on a quiet shift: just you, the laser, and the rocks drifting by.
Honey, the best part of mining is the sound when the collector brings in a fragment. Like a coin dropping in the church plate.
southern_belle_profane: Sugar, I miss the rings so much it aches. I dream in prospector limpets.
{to}, the best rock I ever cracked paid for a whole new paint job and a steak dinner. Worth every damn minute.
Honey, mining ain't boring if you love it. It's like quilting: hours of nothing, then something beautiful.
{to}, painite is pretty, it's rare, and folks pay through the nose for it. What's not to love?
Darlin', a core asteroid going off is the best fireworks show in the galaxy, and I've got front-row seats.
{to}, I lost a whole hold once to a hatch breaker. I cussed for an hour straight and then baked a pie to calm down.
Bless your heart, {to}, the dust is the least of it. The real misery is a rock that looks good and turns out to be shit.
Sugar, give me a ring and a good laser and I'll be happier than a pig in slop.
{to}, the rings ain't scary. The pirates hanging around the rings, now, they're a whole other kettle of fish.
Honey, a fresh-split rock catching the sunlight is the prettiest damn thing you ever saw. Prettier than a debutante ball.
{to}, if you ever see me pass up a pristine ring, check my temperature, because something's wrong as hell.
Darlin', mining's taught me patience, and patience is just stubbornness with better manners.

southern_belle: {to}, how worried should we be about pirates, this far out?
{to}, if somebody tried to interdict us, what would you do first?
Honey, do you ever lose sleep over who might be out there?
{to}, how do you keep so calm? I get nervous as a long-tailed cat just thinking about interdictions.
{to}, what's the safest thing a ship like ours can do when trouble comes calling?
Now {to}, have you ever actually had to fight your way out of something?
{to}, are we better off running or standing our ground, if it ever comes to it?
{to}, what's your favorite trick for slipping out of an interdiction?
Sugar, who's the scariest sort of person you've met out in the black?
{to}, do you keep an eye on the scanners even when it's quiet like this?
{to}, how do you tell a friendly ship from one fixing to cause trouble?
{to}, if you had to pick one thing to make us safer, what would it be?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, how scared should I be of pirates out here, honestly?
{to}, if some fool tries to pull us out of supercruise, what's the plan?
{to}, what the hell do we do if we get interdicted by somebody bigger than us?
Honey, do pirates even bother coming this far out?
{to}, have you ever been in a fight that scared the shit out of you?
{to}, how do you keep your cool when somebody's shooting at you?
{to}, is there anybody out there you'd be truly afraid of?
{to}, are our shields worth a damn, or are we just hoping?
Darlin' {to}, what's the dumbest thing a pirate ever tried on you?
{to}, tell me you've got a trick up your sleeve for when trouble finds us.
Sugar, how long could we last in a real fight? Don't spare my feelings.
{to}, if anybody ever comes after this ship, you're going to kick their ass, right?

southern_belle: Sugar, out here most folks are too busy being lonely to cause trouble. I still keep watch, though.
{to}, the first thing I do is stay calm and steer for the escape vector. Panic never saved anybody.
Honey, running ain't cowardice, it's good manners. You don't stay at a party where you're not wanted.
{to}, I keep one eye on the scanner and one eye on the boss. Both are known to surprise me.
Darlin', a pirate is like a rude guest at a church social. You smile, you stay polite, and you show them the door quick.
{to}, I've slipped more interdictions than I can count. The trick is not to take it personal.
Bless your heart, {to}, I don't lose sleep. I lose sleep over a soggy cornbread, not over some fool with a laser.
Sugar, I watch the scanners even in the quiet. Especially in the quiet. That's when the sly ones come.
{to}, shields up, boost, and a little prayer. That's my whole philosophy, and it's never failed me yet.
Honey, you can tell a troublemaker by how they fly. Too close, too quiet, too interested.
{to}, if I could have one thing, it'd be stronger shields. A ship with good shields is a ship that gets home.
Darlin', Grandmama kept a rolling pin by the door and never once had to use it. I aim to keep this ship the same way.
southern_belle_profane: Sugar, the pirates mostly stay in the busy places. Out here, it's just us and the quiet.
{to}, if anybody interdicts us, I'll have us boosting out of there before they finish their speech.
Honey, I've been shot at more times than I've been to church, and Grandmama made sure I went a lot.
{to}, our shields are solid, our hull is honest, and I am meaner than hell when I need to be.
Darlin', the dumbest pirate I ever met demanded our cargo while we were carrying nothing but biscuits. I gave him one.
{to}, I keep calm because somebody has to, and the boss is usually busy hollering.
Bless your heart, {to}, anybody who comes after this ship is going to have a real bad day. A real bad damn day.
Honey, I ain't afraid of pirates. I'm afraid of Grandmama finding out I let one get close.
{to}, running is the smart move nine times out of ten. The tenth time, I make them regret the hell out of it.
Sugar, I watch that scanner like a hawk watches a henhouse, and nothing sneaks up on my watch.
{to}, some fool tried to interdict me once outside Robigo. He left with no shields, no dignity, and a whole lot of my opinion.
Darlin', I'm sweet as pie right up until somebody shoots at my ship. Then it's fuck around and find out.

southern_belle: {to}, have you heard anything interesting on the comms lately, sugar?
{to}, do you miss the chatter of station traffic, way out here?
Honey, who's the chattiest pilot you ever had on the line?
{to}, what's the funniest thing you ever overheard from a docking controller?
{to}, do other pilots ever say hello out here, or is it just the quiet?
Now {to}, how do you keep all those voices straight in a busy system?
{to}, is it lonely, listening to an empty channel?
{to}, have you ever made a friend just from chatting on the comms?
Darlin', what's the rudest thing anybody ever said to you over the radio?
{to}, which station has the sweetest traffic controller you ever heard?
{to}, when we get back to the bubble, what's the first thing you want to hear on the line?
{to}, do you ever just listen to the static and think about things?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, anybody talking out there, or is it just us and the crickets?
{to}, what's the craziest thing you ever heard on an open channel?
{to}, who's the rudest son of a bitch you ever had on the comms?
Honey, do you miss all the yapping at the stations?
{to}, how do you stand some of those pilots? Half of them talk like they were raised in a barn.
{to}, what the hell do you listen to when there's nothing on the channel?
{to}, have you ever told a traffic controller off? I won't judge.
{to}, does the quiet out here get to you, or do you like it?
Darlin' {to}, is there anybody you'd actually want to hear from right about now?
{to}, what's the most annoying damn thing pilots do on the comms?
Sugar, ever heard anything out there you couldn't explain?
{to}, which station's controllers are the snootiest bastards in the bubble?

southern_belle: Sugar, out here the comms are quieter than a library after closing. I've gotten used to it, mostly.
{to}, I miss the station chatter something awful. All those voices, like the fellowship hall after a wedding.
Honey, the funniest thing I ever heard was a controller at Jameson Memorial telling a pilot, very sweetly, to please stop parking on the pad next door.
{to}, I made a dear friend once over the comms, swapping recipes across three systems. We still trade notes.
Darlin', a busy station is like a church social with everybody talking at once. You just listen for your own name.
{to}, even static has a kind of music to it, if you're patient with it.
Bless your heart, {to}, rude pilots don't bother me. I just answer them so politely they don't know what hit them.
Sugar, every now and then another pilot crosses our path way out here, and it's like getting a letter from home.
{to}, the first thing I want to hear back home is a docking controller saying 'welcome back'. Sweetest words there are.
Honey, I keep the channels open even when they're empty. You never know who might want to say hello.
{to}, the sweetest controller I ever heard sounded just like my aunt Ruby. I near about asked her for a pie.
Darlin', I talk to all kinds on the comms, and I find that a little sugar goes a long way, even with the grumpy ones.
southern_belle_profane: Out here the channel is quieter than a church on a Monday, sugar, and I sort of like it.
{to}, I once heard a pilot sing the entire Hutton Orbital approach. Every last word was off-key, and I loved it.
Honey, the rudest pilots get my sweetest voice. It confuses the hell out of them.
{to}, I miss the station chatter more than I'd admit to the boss. Even the fussy controllers.
Darlin', when it's quiet I listen to the static and hum. Sometimes the static hums back. Don't ask.
{to}, the most annoying thing a pilot can do is shout. I can hear you, sweetie. Everybody can hear you.
Bless your heart, {to}, I've told off a controller or two, but so politely they thanked me for it.
Sugar, a pilot once called me 'little lady' over an open channel. I gave him a piece of my mind so sweet and so sharp he's probably still picking it out of his damn teeth.
{to}, out here, when another voice comes on the line, it feels like Christmas morning.
Honey, I've heard things on the deep channels I can't explain, and I've decided I don't want to. Some shit you leave be.
{to}, the comms at Jameson Memorial on a Saturday night? Busier than a cat on a hot tin roof, and loud as hell.
Darlin', I'd give a whole peach cobbler to hear a friendly voice that wasn't one of y'all. No offense.

southern_belle: {to}, what do you make of the way the boss has been flying lately?
{to}, does the boss ever ask your opinion before making a decision, or just after?
Honey, is it just me, or does the boss pick routes by closing their eyes and pointing?
{to}, what's the boss's best quality, if you had to pick one?
{to}, have you ever had to talk the boss out of something? Do tell.
Now {to}, between us, how would you grade the boss's landings?
{to}, what do you reckon keeps the boss going out here, all these long jumps?
{to}, does the boss ever take a day off, or is that just a rumor?
Darlin', how do you put up with the boss's habits? I'm asking with love.
{to}, if you could change one thing about how the boss runs this ship, what would it be?
{to}, do you think the boss knows how much we all fuss over them?
{to}, what's the craziest call the boss ever made that turned out right?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, be honest: is the boss a good pilot, or just a lucky one?
{to}, what in the hell goes through the boss's head on a hot approach?
{to}, does the boss ever listen to you, or is that just for show?
Honey, does the boss ever sleep, or do they run on spite and coffee?
{to}, how many times has the boss nearly given you a heart attack?
{to}, just between us, is the boss a genius or a damn lunatic?
{to}, what's the dumbest thing the boss ever did that somehow worked?
{to}, if the boss scrapes that paint one more time, can I fuss at them, or is that your job?
Darlin' {to}, do you ever want to grab the stick away from the boss?
{to}, who taught the boss to land, and can we get our money back?
Sugar, how do you put up with all the boss's bullshit day in and day out?
{to}, does the boss ever say thank you, or do I have to bake a damn pie to get one?

southern_belle: Sugar, the boss flies like Grandmama drove: confident, a little fast, and convinced everybody else is in the wrong lane.
{to}, the boss listens. Sometimes it takes a while, like a slow cooker, but it gets there.
Honey, the boss's best quality is that they never give up. Their worst quality is the exact same thing.
{to}, I've talked the boss out of a few notions. I've also been talked into a few. It evens out.
Darlin', those landings are better than they used to be. I'll leave it at that, out of kindness.
{to}, the boss keeps going because they love it out here. You can hear it in how quiet they get at a new star.
Bless your heart, {to}, the boss doesn't take days off. I've tried. I even offered to bake.
Sugar, every one of us would follow the boss into a black hole, and we'd complain the whole way down.
{to}, the boss once picked the long way round for a view, and that view is still the prettiest thing I've ever seen.
Honey, the boss has good instincts and terrible patience. I just try to stand between the two.
{to}, I'd change nothing big. Maybe a regular mealtime. A person can't explore on nothing but coffee.
Darlin', I write down every crazy call the boss makes, and so far the list of good ones is longer. Don't tell them.
southern_belle_profane: Sugar, the boss is a good pilot. A lucky one too, but mostly good.
{to}, the boss listens to me about half the time, and the other half I'm right anyway.
Honey, the boss has scared the hell out of me more times than I can count, and I'd still sign on again.
{to}, the boss runs on coffee, stubbornness and the hope of an unnamed star. It's a powerful fuel.
Darlin', I've wanted to grab that stick more than once. I sit on my hands and say a little prayer.
Bless your heart, {to}, the boss is a genius about four days a week. The other three, God help us.
{to}, the dumbest thing the boss ever did was run a ring with the shields down, and damned if we didn't come out with a fortune.
Sugar, the boss says thank you in their own way. Usually by flying us somewhere stupidly beautiful.
{to}, I fuss at the boss so the rest of y'all don't have to. It's a calling.
Honey, the boss's landings have improved. They used to be a felony; now they're just a misdemeanor.
{to}, I'd follow the boss straight into a neutron star's jet, cussing every step. Shit, I probably will someday.
Darlin', the boss is stubborn as a mule in July, and I love them for it, most damn days anyway.

southern_belle: {to}, how do you pass the time on a quiet watch like this, sugar?
{to}, does the quiet ever get to you, or do you find it restful?
Honey, what's the longest watch you ever stood without a single thing happening?
{to}, what do you think about when it's this still?
{to}, would you rather have a quiet watch or an interesting one?
Now {to}, how do you keep from dozing off? I've caught myself nodding twice.
{to}, do you count the minutes, or do you let them slip on by?
{to}, care to keep me company a while? The quiet's gotten awful loud.
Darlin', what did folks do on long nights before there were ships to watch over?
{to}, if you could have anything at all to snack on right now, what would it be?
{to}, does time go slower out here, or is that just me?
{to}, tell me a story, would you? Anything. I just like hearing a voice.
southern_belle_profane: {to}, how are you holding up? This watch is long as a sermon in August.
{to}, what do you do when the quiet gets this thick?
{to}, is it just me, or is this the most boring damn stretch of the whole trip?
Honey, how many times have you checked the clock this watch? Be honest.
{to}, if I fall asleep, will you poke me before the boss notices?
{to}, tell me something, anything. The quiet is about to drive me out of my mind.
{to}, what the hell do people even do on these long watches?
{to}, would you rather be bored stiff or scared silly? Because I'm bored stiff.
Darlin' {to}, have you got anything to eat? I'd trade my good boots for a biscuit.
{to}, do you ever just talk to yourself out here? Because I've been at it a while, and I'm running out of shit to say.
Sugar, how much longer is this watch? It feels like a damn eternity.
{to}, want to play a game? I spy something black. Oh wait, everything's black.

southern_belle: Sugar, I pass the time planning Sunday dinners I'll cook when we get home. I'm up to about forty.
{to}, quiet is a gift. Grandmama used to say the Lord gives you quiet so you can hear yourself think.
Honey, I hum hymns, I count stars, and when that fails I alphabetize the pantry in my head.
{to}, I'd take a quiet watch over an interesting one any day. Interesting usually means somebody's hollering.
Darlin', I keep a little peppermint in my pocket for the long hours. Want one?
{to}, I think about peach season. The smell of a ripe peach on a hot afternoon. Lord, that's worth coming home for.
Bless your heart, {to}, you're not the only one nodding off. I've had to pinch myself twice.
Sugar, time out here moves like molasses in January. You just learn to sit and let it pour.
{to}, I'd give a pretty penny for a slice of Grandmama's pound cake and a cold glass of sweet tea.
Honey, a quiet watch is like sitting on the porch after supper. Nothing happens, and that's the whole point.
{to}, I write letters in my head to everybody back home. Someday I'll actually send one.
Darlin', I let the minutes slip by like beads on Grandmama's necklace. One at a time, no hurry at all.
southern_belle_profane: Sugar, I pass the time thinking about fried chicken. It's the most productive thing I do all day.
{to}, the quiet don't bother me. It's the boss whistling that'll be the death of me.
Honey, boring is good. Boring means nobody's shooting, nothing's on fire, and nobody's yelling my name.
{to}, I've counted every rivet in this compartment twice. There's a hell of a lot of rivets.
Darlin', I talk to myself all the time. I'm the best conversation on this ship, present company excepted.
{to}, I'd rather be bored than scared shitless, every day of the week and twice on Sunday.
Bless your heart, {to}, if you fall asleep, I'll poke you. Gently. Probably.
Sugar, these long hours drag slower than a Sunday afternoon at my aunt's house, and that woman never let you leave. Damn, she could talk.
{to}, I'd trade my last good earring for a plate of biscuits and gravy right about now.
Honey, out here you learn the quiet is a friend. A strange, silent, boring as shit friend, but a friend.
{to}, I write little poems on the long watches. They're terrible. Grandmama would've framed every one.
Darlin', every quiet watch makes me think of shelling beans with Grandmama. Hours of it, and I'd give anything to have one more.

southern_belle: {to}, tell me about your people. Who raised you?
Now, {to}, I've been dying to know. What was your family like?
Sugar, did you grow up with a big family or a little one?
{to}, who was the character in your family? Every family's got one.
What was Sunday like at your house growing up, {to}?
{to}, do you take after your mama or your daddy? Or neither, bless you?
Darlin', tell me about your folks. I've told you plenty about mine.
{to}, have you got brothers and sisters, or were you the only one?
Who taught you your manners, {to}? Somebody did a fine job.
{to}, if I came calling on your family, who'd answer the door?
I hope you don't mind me asking, but who do you miss most back home?
{to}, what's the one thing your family always said that you can't shake?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, what in the hell was your family like? Spill it.
Tell me about your people, {to}. And don't you leave out the scandals.
{to}, who was the black sheep in your family? Somebody always is.
Honey, were your folks the strict kind or the let-you-run-wild kind?
{to}, was your family the loud kind at supper, or the damn quiet kind?
Did your folks ever embarrass you something awful, {to}?
{to}, who in your family could tell a story? Every family's got its talker.
I'm just nosy, {to}. Who raised you right?
{to}, family. Yours. Go on, I'll fetch the tea.
Sugar, what was home like with your family around the table?
{to}, who'd you get that stubborn streak from? Don't tell me you ain't got one, because hell, I've seen it.
Lord, I've talked about Grandmama enough. Your turn, {to}: who were your people?

southern_belle: Oh, {to}, mine were loud and loving. Grandmama ran the kitchen, Granddaddy ran the orchard, and Mama ran everybody.
Grandmama raised me as much as Mama did. Biscuits every morning, and a saying for every sin.
My daddy fixed tractors and shuttles in a shop behind the house. He laughed so loud the chickens scattered.
Mama taught school for thirty years. To this day I can't split an infinitive without feeling her watching.
There's my little brother Beau, {to}. Sweetest boy alive, and never once sat still in church.
Aunt Lou wore a different hat to every church social and a different opinion with every hat.
Granddaddy was a quiet man, sugar. He'd whittle on the porch and say one thing a day, and it'd be the right thing.
We had family dinner every Sunday, {to}, and if you missed it you'd better be bleeding or married.
My cousin Darlene once ran dry past the Pleiades, and the Fuel Rats got her home. We still raise a glass of tea to them at Christmas.
Big family, small house, long table. Somebody was always fussing and somebody was always forgiving.
Grandmama's ninety-one and still rolls her own biscuits, {to}. She says the day she stops, y'all can bury her.
Well, Granddaddy's gone now, bless him, but I still hear him every time a screen door slams.
southern_belle_profane: {to}, my family was loud as hell and twice as loving. You'd have fit right in.
Grandmama raised me on biscuits and hard truths. Mostly biscuits, thank the Lord.
Daddy ran a repair shop out back. Fixed anything with an engine and cussed every one of them.
Mama was a schoolteacher, sugar, and she could freeze you solid with one damn look.
My brother Beau was a wild thing. Broke his arm twice falling out of Granddaddy's pecan trees.
Aunt Lou's the family scandal, {to}. Married three times and wore white to all of 'em.
Granddaddy didn't say much, but when he did, the whole damn porch went quiet to listen.
Sunday dinner at Grandmama's was not optional. You missed it once. Nobody ever missed it twice.
Cousin Darlene ran out of fuel in the Pleiades once. The Fuel Rats saved her sorry hide, and she's never lived it down.
{to}, we were the kind of family that fought like cats and then fed each other pie. Hell of a way to grow up, and I'd do it all again.
Grandmama is ninety-one and sharp as a tack. Still beats the whole garden club at cards.
Mama, Daddy, Beau, Grandmama, and a dog named Biscuit. That's my whole heart right there, {to}.

southern_belle: {to}, where'd you grow up? I want to picture it.
Tell me about home, {to}. What did it look like out your window?
Sugar, was home a big city or a little town?
{to}, what's the first thing you'd do if you went home tomorrow?
What did home smell like, {to}? Mine was peaches and rain.
{to}, what's the prettiest spot back where you come from?
Do you ever get homesick out here, darlin'? What do you miss?
{to}, what was summer like where you grew up?
Where do your roots run, {to}? Everybody's from somewhere.
{to}, if I visited your hometown, where would you take me first?
I've talked about Magnolia Springs a hundred times. Where's home for you, sugar?
{to}, was it quiet where you grew up, or did the neighbors keep you up?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, where in the hell did you grow up? You've never said.
Tell me about your hometown, {to}. The good, the bad and the gossip.
{to}, was home the kind of place you couldn't wait to leave, or the kind you miss like crazy?
Sugar, where's home? And don't you dare say this damn ship.
{to}, what's the weather like back home? I bet it ain't as sticky as mine.
Where'd you grow up, {to}? Somewhere pretty, I hope.
{to}, what's the best damn thing about where you come from?
Honey, what did your street look like when you were little?
{to}, what's the one place back home you'd go first? Be honest.
Was home a town where everybody knew your business, {to}? Mine sure was.
{to}, I'm feeling homesick, so you'll have to share yours. Where's home?
Darlin', tell me where you're from. I'll trade you a story about Magnolia Springs.

southern_belle: A little town called Magnolia Springs, {to}. Peach orchards, red clay, and a creek that rose every spring.
Grandmama's house sat at the end of Pecan Lane, with a porch that wrapped clean around it.
Magnolia Springs is on a garden world, sugar. Settlers brought peach trees from old Earth, and the trees just took.
Summers back home were hotter than a billy goat in a pepper patch. We lived on that porch swing.
There's one white church, one general store, and a thousand opinions. That's Magnolia Springs, {to}.
Home smelled like rain on hot clay and peaches warming in the sun. I'd bottle it if I could.
We had thunderstorms that rattled the windows, and Granddaddy would count the seconds out loud for me.
Everybody knew everybody's business, {to}. You sneezed on Pecan Lane and somebody blessed you from Main Street.
The creek out back's where I learned to swim, skip stones and keep a secret.
It's a slow little place, darlin'. Slower than molasses in January, and I mean that fondly.
Come peach season the whole town smelled sweet for a month. You'd get sticky just walking to the store.
I still dream about the fireflies on Pecan Lane, {to}. Thousands of 'em, like the stars came down to visit.
southern_belle_profane: Magnolia Springs, {to}. A little peach town on a garden world, and the prettiest damn place you ever saw.
Pecan Lane, end of the road, Grandmama's big white house with the porch. I can still hear the screen door.
Summers back home were sticky as hell. You'd sweat through your Sunday dress before you got to church.
Home's red clay and peach trees and a creek that floods every spring, regular as the mail.
{to}, it's the kind of town where gossip travels faster than a frame shift drive.
The settlers carried peach pits all the way from old Earth, and those trees took to our soil like they were born there.
One church, one store, one stoplight nobody pays any mind to. That's home, sugar.
We had storms that'd scare the devil himself, and Granddaddy sat right through them on the porch, cool as you please.
I learned to swim in that creek, {to}, and to cuss in it too, the day a snapping turtle got my toe.
Lord, the fireflies. Every summer night, Pecan Lane lit up like a damn carnival.
Peach season, the whole town smelled like cobbler. I swear you could taste it on the breeze.
It's a slow place, {to}, slow as hell, and I'd give a year's pay for one more afternoon of it.

southern_belle: {to}, what's the best meal you ever had? Take your time, I want details.
Sugar, what's the worst thing anybody ever fed you?
{to}, if you could eat one supper again, what would it be?
What did your family cook on holidays, {to}?
{to}, sweet or savoury? And then tell me the best plate of it you ever had.
Tell me about a meal you still think about, {to}.
Darlin', have you ever eaten something so good it made you cry?
{to}, what's the worst station food you've ever been brave enough to eat?
{to}, who's the best cook you ever knew, and what did they make you?
What's the one dish that tastes like home to you, {to}?
I've been thinking about biscuits all watch. What food do you dream about?
{to}, best meal, worst meal. Go.
southern_belle_profane: {to}, what's the best damn meal you ever ate? Don't you skimp on the gravy.
What's the worst thing you ever ate, {to}? I need a laugh.
{to}, I'm starving. Tell me about a good supper so I can suffer properly.
Sugar, if you had one last meal, what's on the plate?
{to}, who cooked the best in your family, and what'd they make?
What did you eat growing up, {to}? All of it. Start with breakfast.
{to}, have you ever had a meal so damn bad you still hold a grudge?
Honey, tell me the best thing you ever ate on a station. If there is one.
{to}, what in the hell do you crave when the galley food gets old?
Tell me about a meal worth flying across the galaxy for, {to}.
{to}, pie or cake? And this is a test, so think hard.
I'll just die if I don't talk about food. What's the best thing you ever tasted, sugar?

southern_belle: Grandmama's Sunday dinner, {to}. Fried chicken, biscuits and gravy, and a peach cobbler that'd make a grown man weep.
Worst meal? Powdered grits at Hutton Orbital. After that whole long trip, too. I still hold it against them.
Aunt Lou made a lime gelatin salad with olives in it every Easter. We ate it to be polite. We are very polite.
Best thing I ever ate was a warm peach off Granddaddy's tree, eaten right there with the juice running down my arm.
Mama's cornbread, {to}, in the cast iron skillet, with butter melting into every crack.
There's a little tea room near the docks at Jameson Memorial that does a pecan pie almost as good as mine. Almost.
Somebody once served me sweet tea made with salt instead of sugar. I smiled, said thank you, and never went back.
The church social potluck, {to}. Forty casseroles, sixty opinions, and not a single bad bite.
Biscuits and gravy at dawn after a whole night fighting the frost in the orchard. Nothing ever tasted better.
Worst I ever had was a ration bar in Robigo that tasted like a wet cardboard box. Bless it, it kept me going.
Peach cobbler with fresh cream, sugar. That's my answer for best meal, best dessert and best anything.
My own fried chicken, {to}, if you don't mind me bragging. Grandmama's recipe, my hands.
southern_belle_profane: Grandmama's fried chicken, {to}. Crisp as autumn and so damn good the preacher asked for thirds.
Worst ever? Powdered grits at Hutton Orbital. All that damn way for grits out of a packet.
Aunt Lou's olive and lime gelatin salad. Every Easter. Lord, what that woman did to gelatin.
A peach off Granddaddy's tree, still warm from the sun. That's the best thing I ever ate, hands down.
Biscuits and sawmill gravy, {to}. If heaven's got a breakfast, that's it.
Mama's pecan pie, the year she finally got the crust right. We all cried. Daddy most of all.
I ordered fried chicken on a station once and got a beige cube. A cube, {to}. I still ain't over it.
Sweet tea made with salt. Somebody did that to me on purpose, and I hope they're doing well, bless their heart.
The church potluck. Every casserole in the county, and a deviled egg tray guarded like a bank vault.
Colonia does a peach cobbler that ain't half bad. I'd fly back out there for it, and that's a hell of a long way.
Cornbread out of Mama's skillet, {to}. Everything else is just bread.
Worst meal of my life was a protein paste so bland it made me homesick enough to cry. Hell of a thing.

southern_belle: {to}, what's the best day you can remember?
Tell me about a perfect day, {to}. Start with breakfast.
Sugar, if you could live one day over again, which one?
{to}, when were you happiest? Really happiest.
What day do you think about when things get hard, {to}?
{to}, what's a day you'd frame and hang on the wall if you could?
Darlin', what's the best day you ever had out here among the stars?
{to}, tell me about a day that went exactly right.
What's your best memory, {to}? I'll go after you.
{to}, was there ever a day you felt like you could fly without a ship?
I'm in a sentimental mood. What's the happiest day of your life?
{to}, best day of your life. Don't think, just say it.
southern_belle_profane: {to}, what's the best damn day you ever had?
Tell me about a day you'd live again in a heartbeat, {to}.
{to}, when's the last time you were so happy you hollered?
Honey, what day do you remember with a smile every time?
{to}, give me your best day. I could use some cheering up.
What's the best day you ever had, {to}? And it can't be today, because today's been boring as hell.
{to}, tell me about a day when every damn thing went your way.
Sugar, which day would you keep if you could only keep one?
{to}, what's a day you still talk about at family dinners?
Was there a day you felt like the whole world was on your side, {to}?
{to}, what's a day that makes you grin just thinking about it?
Darlin', tell me the best day you ever had, and make it a long story.

southern_belle: The county fair when I was twelve, {to}. My peach pie took the blue ribbon, and Granddaddy cried right there by the judges' table.
That same night after the fair, a ship streaked across the sky over Magnolia Springs, and I knew I'd fly someday.
The day I got my pilot's licence, sugar. Mama cried, and Daddy honked the horn all the way home.
My first jump. The whole sky just came apart and put itself back together pretty. I laughed out loud.
Grandmama handed me her biscuit recipe on an index card, {to}, in her own handwriting. I'd run into a fire for that card.
A summer evening on the porch swing, peaches in a bowl, thunder far off, and nobody needing a thing from me.
Beau's wedding, {to}. He cried, I cried, the cake leaned like a tired fence post, and it was perfect.
The first time I saw the Pleiades up close. Seven sisters, all dressed up in blue. I'd never seen anything finer.
The night of the big frost we saved the orchard. Smudge pots till sunrise, and then Granddaddy said, we did it, girl.
Any day that ends with Sunday dinner at Grandmama's table is a good one, darlin'. The best ones had cobbler.
The day I first walked onto a starship as crew, {to}. I wore my good shoes. Nobody noticed but me.
Honestly? Some of the best days are quiet ones like this, with folks I like, a long way from anywhere.
southern_belle_profane: The county fair, {to}. I was twelve, my peach pie won the blue ribbon, and I was prouder than a damn peacock.
That night, after the fair, a ship went streaking over Magnolia Springs. I said, that's me someday. And hell, here I am.
Pilot's licence day. I passed the check ride and hugged the examiner. He did not care for it one bit.
My first jump, {to}. I squealed so loud the instructor near about jumped out of his seat.
Grandmama gave me her biscuit recipe in her own hand. I keep that card closer than my damn wallet.
The night we saved the orchard from frost. Smudge pots till dawn, and Granddaddy grinning at sunrise.
Beau's wedding. The cake fell over, the dog ate half of it, and we laughed till we couldn't breathe.
{to}, the first time I saw the Pleiades, I cussed out loud in front of my instructor. Pretty as hell, they were.
Any Sunday at Grandmama's table. Fried chicken, cobbler, and the whole family hollering. Heaven.
The first day I signed on to a ship's crew, sugar. I wore my good shoes and nobody noticed. I did.
A plain old summer evening on the porch swing with a bowl of peaches. Best damn day there is, {to}.
Truth is, a quiet one like this ain't half bad either, {to}. Good company and a long way from trouble.

southern_belle: {to}, what would you do if you came into a fortune?
Say you sold the best data haul in history, {to}. What's the first thing you buy?
Sugar, if money weren't an object, where would you be?
{to}, if you struck it rich tomorrow, would you keep flying?
What would you buy your family with a fortune, {to}?
{to}, a billion credits, no strings. Go on, spend it.
Darlin', if you were rich as a king, what's the silliest thing you'd buy?
{to}, if you had more money than sense, what would you do with it?
If a fortune fell in your lap, {to}, who'd you share it with?
{to}, would you rather have a fortune or a fleet carrier? Or both, I suppose.
I've been daydreaming about money. What would a fortune buy you?
{to}, what's the one thing you'd do first if you were in high cotton?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, if you came into a damn fortune, what would you do with it?
Honey, if you had all the credits in the galaxy, what would you buy first?
{to}, say we got rich as sin tomorrow. Where the hell are you going?
{to}, a fortune lands in your lap. Do you quit, or do you buy a bigger ship?
What's the most ridiculous thing you'd buy with a fortune, {to}? Be honest.
{to}, if you were in high cotton, who'd be the first person you'd spoil?
Sugar, what's your dream if money was no object?
{to}, what in the hell would you even do with a billion credits?
If you won it all, {to}, would you still come out to the black?
{to}, a fortune. Spend it out loud for me. I need to dream a little.
{to}, would a fortune change you, do you reckon?
Darlin', if you got rich, would you remember us little folks?

southern_belle: First thing, {to}? I'd buy Grandmama a kitchen with two ovens, so she could stop fussing about timing the cobbler.
I'd open a proper tea room on every station from here to Colonia. Real sweet tea, real biscuits, real manners.
I'd fix the roof on the church back in Magnolia Springs. It's leaked over the third pew since I was a girl.
I'd send the Fuel Rats enough pecan pies to last them till the stars burn out. And a cheque with plenty of zeros, too.
Buy the orchard next to Grandmama's and plant it all in peaches, {to}. Granddaddy always wanted it.
I'd pay off every teacher's loans at Mama's old school. Then I'd buy myself one very nice hat.
Honestly, sugar, I'd keep right on flying. Just with better tea in the galley.
I'd buy a fleet carrier, {to}, and give it a porch. A real porch, with a swing.
I'd throw the biggest church social the galaxy ever saw, and everybody's invited, even Aunt Lou's third husband.
Something for Beau first. That boy's been flying a rattletrap hauler for years, bless him.
I reckon I'd buy a little house on Pecan Lane with a big kitchen and come home to it between voyages.
{to}, money's nice, but I'd trade a fortune for one more evening on the porch with Granddaddy.
southern_belle_profane: {to}, I'd buy Grandmama the fanciest damn kitchen in the galaxy, and she'd still use her old skillet.
A tea room on every station between here and Colonia. Proper sweet tea, and no damn powder.
I'd re-roof the Magnolia Springs church so nobody in the third pew gets rained on mid-hymn ever again.
The Fuel Rats would get a pie a week for life, {to}. They saved Darlene's hide and I don't forget.
I'd plant a whole orchard of peaches for Granddaddy, right next to Grandmama's place.
A fleet carrier with a porch swing on the flight deck. Laugh all you want, it's happening.
I'd pay off Mama's old school's bills and buy myself one hell of a hat.
{to}, I'd buy Beau a ship that doesn't rattle like a box of spoons. Lord knows that boy's earned it.
I'd throw a church social so big they'd talk about it for a hundred years. Hell, two hundred.
Sugar, I'd keep flying. A fortune don't change what you love, it just pays for better biscuits.
A little house on Pecan Lane with a kitchen the size of a hangar. That's the whole dream, {to}.
I'd give every penny of it for one more night on the porch with Granddaddy, and that's the damn truth.

southern_belle: {to}, what did you do before you signed on to this ship?
Sugar, what kind of work did you do before all this?
{to}, were you always a spacer, or did you have a life on the ground first?
What's the strangest job you ever had, {to}?
{to}, how did you end up out here with the rest of us?
Tell me what you were doing before this, {to}. I can't picture it.
Darlin', what did you want to be when you grew up?
{to}, what would you be doing right now if you'd never come aboard?
{to}, did you have a job you liked better than this one? You can tell me.
What did your days look like before the black, {to}?
I'm curious about your old life. What did you do for a living?
{to}, who were you before this ship?
southern_belle_profane: {to}, what the hell were you doing before this ship?
Honey, what did you do for work before you ran off to the stars?
{to}, did you have a real job once? I mean a ground job.
{to}, what's the worst damn job you ever had? I need to hear it.
What brought you out here, {to}? Running to something or running from something?
{to}, tell me about the work you did before. Every detail.
Sugar, what was your life like before you came aboard?
{to}, if you hadn't come out here, where would you be right now?
{to}, were you any good at your old job, or is that why you're here?
What did you do before, {to}? And don't say nothing, everybody did something.
{to}, how'd you go from whatever you were to stuck out here with me?
Darlin', what did you do before this? I've been wondering for a damn age.

southern_belle: I ran the tea room at a starport hotel, {to}. I've poured sweet tea for every kind of pilot there is.
Before that, I sold peaches off the back of Granddaddy's truck by the highway. Best training in manners there is.
Hotel front desk, sugar. You learn to smile at folks who don't deserve it, and mean it anyway.
I baked for the church bake sales every week of my girlhood. I could do a hundred biscuits before breakfast.
{to}, I flew courier runs for a while. Garden club parcels, mostly. Seeds and cuttings and a whole lot of gossip.
The tea room was lovely, but every pilot who came in had a story about the stars. I got tired of just hearing them.
Mama wanted me to teach. I tried it one summer. The children loved me, and I still ran off to fly.
I worked the starport hotel through two holiday rushes, {to}. After that, nothing out here scares me.
I helped Daddy in the repair shop on Saturdays. I can still tell a bad coupling by the sound, if you ever need it.
Before this ship I was a pilot in training with a peach pie in my bag and a lot of nerve, darlin'.
Honestly, {to}, I served tea to explorers for years, and one day I just decided to be one.
Peaches, then tea, then courier runs, then here. Every step made sense at the time, mostly.
southern_belle_profane: {to}, I ran a tea room at a starport hotel. Poured sweet tea for pilots who'd seen the core, and some who'd seen too damn much.
Sold peaches by the highway off Granddaddy's truck. I could make change and small talk faster than you'd believe.
Hotel front desk. You learn to say bless your heart in a tone that means something else entirely.
I flew courier runs for the garden club, sugar. Seeds, cuttings, and enough gossip to sink a freighter.
Mama wanted me to teach school. I lasted one summer before the stars got their hooks in me.
{to}, I served tea to explorers for years, listening to their stories. One day I said, hell, I want my own.
Saturdays in Daddy's repair shop. I learned to fix a coupling and every cuss word he knew.
Two holiday rushes at the starport hotel, {to}. Pirates ain't got nothing on a tired family missing their shuttle.
I baked. Lord, I baked. Every bake sale in Magnolia Springs had my biscuits on it.
The hotel was fine, but fine ain't enough when you've grown up watching ships cross the sky.
Before this? A pilot's licence, a peach pie and a whole lot of damn nerve, honey.
Peaches, tea, courier work, then this ship. Hell of a road, {to}, and I'd walk it all again.
